data.narrative:
Tevel Aerobotics, a Series B-stage drone and autonomous systems company, has raised $42.6M to date. The addressable peer universe in Drones & Autonomous comprises eight private companies, including Elroy Air, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and Archer Aviation. No public comparables exist in this narrow sector.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression. Using total capital raised ($43M) as a proxy baseline and applying a Series B-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $81M. This approach reflects typical step-up patterns observed across frontier-tech financings at equivalent progression points. Peer-median analysis could not be applied; while five same-sector peers were identified, none met the threshold of three comparable datapoints when filtered for identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. A broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of business models and commercial maturity within drones and autonomous systems.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $69M to $93M, anchored on the median of $81M. Key uncertainties center on the absence of granular comparables at Tevel's exact stage and valuation tier, and the reliance on a single triangulation method. The range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression output. Investors should weight this valuation pending additional disclosure of revenue, unit economics, or customer concentration, which would enable alternative methods and narrow the range.
